\subsection*{Gaussian Space --- Hermite --- Degree: Results}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a normalized Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_degree}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_degree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $k$, the polynomial obtained by multiplying the $k$th
Hermite polynomial, viewed over $\mathbb R$, by $(k!)^{-1/2}$ has degree $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonvanishing of normalized Hermite polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_ne_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_degree}
\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $k$, the normalized Hermite polynomial of degree $k$ is
not the zero polynomial.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Natural degree of a normalized Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_natDegree}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_natDegree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_degree}
\difficulty{1}
For every nonnegative integer $k$, the polynomial obtained by multiplying the $k$th
Hermite polynomial, viewed over $\mathbb R$, by $(k!)^{-1/2}$ has natural degree $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Degree of an embedded univariate polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_toMvPolynomial}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_toMvPolynomial}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $\sigma$ be a type, let $i\in\sigma$, and let $p$ be a polynomial over $\mathbb R$.
Regard $p$ as a multivariate polynomial in the single variable indexed by $i$. Its total
degree equals the natural degree of $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Total degree of a finite product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_finset_prod_of_ne_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_finset_prod_of_ne_zero}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\sigma$ and $\iota$ be types, let $S$ be a finite subset of $\iota$, and assign a
real multivariate polynomial $P_i$ in variables indexed by $\sigma$ to each $i\in\iota$.
If every $P_i$ with $i\in S$ is nonzero, then the total degree of their product is the
sum of their total degrees.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Total degree of a multivariate Hermite polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial_totalDegree}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial_totalDegree}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_natDegree, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.normalizedHermitePolynomial_ne_zero, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_finset_prod_of_ne_zero, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.totalDegree_toMvPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
For a natural number $n$ and a multi-index $\alpha\colon\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb{N}$,
the total degree of the product of normalized Hermite polynomials with coordinate
degrees $\alpha_i$ is $\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i$.
\end{theorem}
